fix(hooks): the session hook fits its cap; a RAG measured before it was built [P334, P335, P300 addenda]

The SessionStart hook pushed this morning would have delivered its first
2,000 characters and nothing else.

Claude Code caps a hook's stdout at 10,000 characters. Over the cap it saves
the output to a file, passes the path and a 2,000-character preview, and does
not ask Claude to read the file. v1 printed 21,338. I had read the hooks
reference for the schema and stopped at the part I needed: the schema was
right, the delivery was wrong.

The same reference says each hook's output is measured on its own. So the
hook now prints the index in parts - 2547 / 8979 / 8975 / 1370 characters -
with one handler per part and one spare. audit-docs.py runs `--plan` and
fails the push when a part has no handler or exceeds the cap. Verified both
ways: with part 4's handler removed, DRIFT; restored, OK. The text is phrased
as facts rather than commands, per the docs' note on prompt-injection
defences.

Scope, stated plainly: these hooks run in local Claude Code sessions in this
folder. In a claude.ai cloud thread in a Project, repository hooks do not
apply.

Retrieval, measured before building it - recall@5 on 9 real repeats with
known answers, Russian and English:

    BM25                       RU 3/9   EN 8/9
    multilingual MiniLM        RU 4/9   EN 3/9

The Russian BM25 hits each rode on an English token in the sentence. The
English queries were written knowing the answers, so 8/9 is an upper bound.
No per-prompt RAG on this evidence: a retriever that is usually wrong teaches
its reader to skip it. Next experiment, untested: retrieve on the ACTION

code.
